q: A guest assumes Extra Dry is the driest style on the list. Where does it actually sit?
opts: At exactly the same sweetness as Brut
Sweeter than Brut, at 12 to 17 grams per litre
At the sweetest end of the scale
exp: The category names are historical and actively misleading. Sec is sweeter still and Demi-Sec sweeter again, so reading the words as English reverses the truth.

q: How much residual sugar may a wine labelled Brut carry?
exp: Brut is by far the largest category and most houses sit somewhere near the middle of the band. The sugar is there to balance ferocious acidity rather than to read as sweetness.

q: No sugar whatever is added at dosage. Which term appears on the label?
exp: Brut Nature, Pas Dose and Dosage Zero all say the same thing, and the wine may still hold up to 3 grams per litre left from fermentation. Nothing conceals a thin base wine.

q: A guest asks you to walk the dosage scale upward in sweetness. Which sequence do you give them?
opts: Extra Brut, Brut Nature, Extra Dry, Brut, Sec, Doux, Demi-Sec
Brut, Brut Nature, Extra Brut, Sec, Extra Dry, Demi-Sec, Doux
Brut Nature, Extra Brut, Brut, Extra Dry, Sec, Demi-Sec, Doux
Doux, Demi-Sec, Sec, Extra Dry, Brut, Extra Brut, Brut Nature
exp: Seven categories, of which only the two extremes are intuitive. Extra Dry sitting between Brut and Sec is the step that catches almost everyone.

q: A dessert course calls for something distinctly sweet from the region. Which category fits?
opts: Extra Dry, at 12 to 17 grams per litre
Sec, at 17 to 32 grams per litre
Demi-Sec, at 32 to 50 grams per litre
exp: Demi-Sec is the practical dessert style, since Doux above 50 grams is now very rarely made. A Brut against a sweet dish is left tasting sour and hollow.

q: Unlike the Burgundian arrangement, the cru ranking here attaches to what unit?
opts: The estate holdings of an individual producer
The whole village and all its vineyards
One named vineyard parcel inside a village
The vintage in which the fruit was grown
exp: Every hectare inside a Grand Cru commune carries the rank, prime slope and flat land alike. It rewards the address rather than the plot, which is why single-vineyard bottlings are a recent development.

q: How many villages hold Grand Cru status in Champagne?
exp: Seventeen communes sit at the top, with a broader band of Premiers Crus beneath them. Most Grand Cru land lies in the Montagne de Reims and on the Cote des Blancs.

q: The old echelle des crus rated each village on a percentage scale. What figure marked a Grand Cru?
exp: The scale originally fixed the price a grower was paid per kilogram of fruit. It was dropped as a pricing mechanism in the 2000s, but the rankings it produced remain in everyday use.

q: Villages rated between ninety and ninety-nine on that scale earned which designation?
exp: Anything below ninety carried no cru designation at all. A Premier Cru name on a label is a genuine if broad indication of the quality of the raw material.

q: Avize, Cramant and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger are Grand Cru villages celebrated for which grape?
exp: All three sit on the Cote des Blancs, where the chalk lies closest to the surface. Le Mesnil is known for wines so austere in youth that they can need a decade to unwind.

q: Ay and Bouzy carry Grand Cru rank on the strength of which variety?
exp: Both are warm, well-exposed sites for black grapes. Bouzy is also known for a still red bottled under the Coteaux Champenois appellation.

q: Two initials in the small print identify who actually made the wine. A bottle marked NM comes from whom?
opts: A grower using only fruit from vines it farms
A merchant house that buys in grapes
A cooperative that sells its members' wine
A retailer commissioning its own brand
exp: Negociant Manipulant covers almost every famous name: the house buys in fruit and bottles the wine under its own name. The houses own only a fraction of the vineyard they need, so long-term grower contracts are the real foundation of the business.

q: Which code marks a grower who makes and bottles wine from vines they farm themselves?
exp: Recoltant Manipulant is the grower-producer, the source of what the trade calls grower Champagne. The scale is small and the wine usually speaks of one village rather than of a house style.

q: A cooperative vinifies its members' fruit and sells the result under a single brand. Which code applies?
exp: Cooperative de Manipulation. RC is the related case, where an individual grower takes finished wine back from the cooperative and sells it under a personal label.

q: A supermarket commissions Champagne and puts its own brand on the bottle. Which two letters appear?
exp: Marque d'Acheteur, a buyer's own brand. The code says nothing at all about quality, only that the name on the front is not the name of the producer.

q: Where should you look to find that producer code?
opts: Stamped into the base of the bottle
On the front label beside the vintage
In the small print on the label
exp: It is required by law and very easy to miss. The number next to it identifies the individual house, grower or cooperative in the official register.
